questions.stem: Which term describes the stated face amount of a bond that the issuer agrees to repay to the bondholder at maturity?
questions.explanation: Par value (also called face value or principal) is the amount the issuer repays at maturity. The coupon is the periodic interest rate paid on that par amount, not the principal itself.

questions.stem: A debt security issued by the U.S. Treasury with an original maturity of one year or less, sold at a discount and paying no periodic interest, is best described as a:
questions.explanation: Treasury bills are short-term (one year or less) zero-coupon Treasury obligations sold at a discount to face value. Treasury notes (2–10 years) and bonds (over 10 years) pay semiannual interest.

questions.stem: Which of the following best defines a general obligation (GO) bond?
choices: A municipal bond backed by revenues from a specific project such as a toll road
A municipal bond backed by the full faith, credit, and taxing power of the issuing municipality
A corporate bond secured by specific real property of the issuer
A federal agency bond backed by the full faith and credit of the U.S. government
questions.explanation: GO bonds are municipal securities backed by the full faith, credit, and taxing power of the issuer. Revenue bonds, by contrast, are repaid from revenues generated by a specific project or facility.

questions.stem: The risk that a bond issuer will fail to make timely payments of interest or principal is known as:
questions.explanation: Credit risk (also called default risk) is the risk that the issuer will be unable to make required interest or principal payments. Interest rate risk relates to price changes from changes in market rates, not issuer creditworthiness.

questions.stem: Which money market instrument is defined as a short-term, unsecured promissory note issued by a corporation, typically to finance working capital needs?
questions.explanation: Commercial paper is short-term unsecured corporate debt used for working capital. A banker's acceptance is a time draft guaranteed by a bank used in trade finance, not general corporate funding.

questions.stem: A bond feature that allows the issuer to redeem the bond before its scheduled maturity at a specified price is known as:
questions.explanation: A call feature grants the issuer the right to redeem the bond prior to maturity. A put feature gives the holder—not the issuer—the right to demand early redemption.

questions.stem: Which term describes a bond's annual interest payment divided by its current market price?
questions.explanation: Current yield equals annual coupon interest divided by the bond's current market price. Nominal yield is the coupon rate based on par value, not current price.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes an asset-backed security (ABS)?
choices: A debt instrument whose payments are derived from a pool of underlying financial assets such as loans or receivables
A bond secured solely by the general credit of a corporate issuer
An equity interest in a real estate investment trust
A municipal security backed by the taxing authority of a state
questions.explanation: ABS are debt securities whose cash flows are supported by a pool of underlying assets (e.g., auto loans, credit card receivables, mortgages). Unsecured corporate debentures rely only on the issuer's general credit.

questions.stem: Prepayment risk is most closely associated with which type of debt security?
questions.explanation: Prepayment risk arises when underlying mortgage borrowers refinance or repay principal early, shortening the life of mortgage-backed securities. Treasury bills and standard GO bonds do not have prepayment features.

questions.stem: Which statement best defines yield to maturity (YTM)?
choices: The coupon rate stated on the face of the bond
The annual coupon divided by current market price
The total annualized return an investor earns if the bond is held to maturity, assuming all coupons are reinvested at the same rate
The return earned if the bond is called at the earliest call date
questions.explanation: YTM is the total annualized return assuming the bond is held to maturity and coupons are reinvested at the YTM rate. Yield to call assumes redemption at the earliest call date instead.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the relationship between bond prices and prevailing market interest rates?
choices: They move in the same direction
They move together only for callable bonds
questions.explanation: Bond prices and interest rates move inversely: when market rates rise, existing bond prices fall, and vice versa. This inverse relationship is a fundamental concept in fixed income.

questions.stem: A negotiable certificate of deposit (CD) is best defined as:
choices: A time deposit at a bank that can be traded in the secondary market before maturity
An equity interest issued by a federally insured bank
An unsecured short-term obligation of a corporation
A municipal security backed by project revenues
questions.explanation: A negotiable CD is a large-denomination bank time deposit that can be sold in the secondary market prior to maturity. Commercial paper, by contrast, is unsecured corporate short-term debt, not a bank deposit.
